Chapter 9: The Power of Lament and Celebration.
As the last months of the experiment drew near, something unexpected happened—the experimenter kept coming back to the language of lament and celebration found in the Bible. Think about it: those ancient words are packed with raw emotion. Songs of deep sorrow mingle with outbursts of pure joy. There are people crying out in pain one moment, and then dancing in gratitude the next.
But let’s be honest—so many faith communities tend to skip over grief. It’s like everyone wants to fast-forward to the happy parts, to stay focused on the positive and sweep the hard stuff aside.
Instead, the experimenter decided to embrace both. She made room for sadness, disappointment, and even anger, right alongside laughter and delight. There were days when life just felt heavy, and prayers sounded more like sighs than songs. But there were also moments that took her by surprise—a friend’s unexpected kindness, the laughter of a child, or the quiet beauty of a sunrise on a cold winter morning.
One evening, she gathered with a small group of women. They shared their stories—tales of loss, and glimmers of hope. Tears came easily, but so did laughter. And in that space, something important became clear: lament and celebration aren’t opposites. They’re companions, walking side by side. You really need both for a full, honest life of faith.
Most of us don’t realize just how healing it is to actually name our pain—to let ourselves grieve what’s been lost. Those ancient psalms and stories? They actually invite us to feel everything, to bring our joy and our sorrow right into the presence of God.
So, here’s the key takeaway: faith isn’t about pretending everything’s fine. It’s about showing up, messy and wonderful, trusting that—no matter what—you’re held.
